cur:manuscripts-paris-gregory-ministry-s.summary: The top register, headed 'the calling of the apostles', shows Christ summoning Peter and Andrew and the sons of Zebedee from their boats, calling Zacchaeus down from the sycamore tree, and calling Matthew from his table heaped with coins. The next register shows Christ with the rich young man and calling Nathanael beneath the fig tree; healings follow below. In every scene Christ, haloed and in a purple mantle, takes the initiative of the call.
facts: Many of its full-page miniatures do not illustrate Gregory's sermons directly but set biblical and historical scenes beside them as a commentary devised for the court.

The Paris Gregory was commissioned by Patriarch Photios as a gift for Emperor Basil I between 879 and 883 and is one of the most ambitious Byzantine manuscripts to survive from the generation after Iconoclasm.
cur:manuscripts-paris-gregory-ministry-s.notes: Folio derived from the Gallica image sequence (view number minus 13, halved) and checked against folios named on other Commons files of this manuscript; the Commons file name gives the Gallica view number, not the folio. The lowest register is damaged and its scenes are not identified here.
